title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Tin (Sn, Z=50) is 118.710(7)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Tin (Sn, Z=50) as 118.710(7), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 50, symbol Sn, as Tin. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Tin as 118.710(7). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Geological materials are known in which the element has an isotopic composition outside the limits for normal material. The difference between the atomic weight of the element in such materials and that given in the table may exceed the stated uncertainty. Isotope rows in the same file: Sn-112 relative atomic mass 111.90482387(61), isotopic composition 0.0097(1); Sn-114 relative atomic mass 113.9027827(10), isotopic composition 0.0066(1); Sn-115 relative atomic mass 114.903344699(16), isotopic composition 0.0034(1); Sn-116 relative atomic mass 115.90174280(10), isotopic composition 0.1454(9); Sn-117 relative atomic mass 116.90295398(52), isotopic composition 0.0768(7); Sn-118 relative atomic mass 117.90160657(54), isotopic composition 0.2422(9); Sn-119 relative atomic mass 118.90331117(78), isotopic composition 0.0859(4); Sn-120 relative atomic mass 119.90220163(97), isotopic composition 0.3258(9); Sn-122 relative atomic mass 121.9034438(26), isotopic composition 0.0463(3); Sn-124 relative atomic mass 123.9052766(11), isotopic composition 0.0579(5). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
